task.title: P6-188: Rewrite delete_collection to relocate rather than destroy
task.description:
Migrated from specs/TODO-Phase-6.md (Stage 1 — Destructive actions and data integrity). Original id: P6-188. Size: M. Specs: specs/collection-deletion.md, specs/collection-api.md.

**Rewrite `delete_collection` to relocate rather than destroy.** Step 3 of specs/collection-deletion.md, and the task that actually closes the data-loss hole. Replace the single `DELETE FROM collections` (`hosted.rs:510`) with: set `deleted_at`; re-point every child's `parent_id` to the deleted collection's parent (children **survive** — delete removes exactly one node); move the holdings out as real ledger moves per the chosen `HaveDisposition` (`ToParent` default, `To`, `ReturnToPrevious` reusing the existing teardown mode, or `Discard`); and apply the chosen `WantDisposition` (`Discard` default, or `To`). **`Discard` writes nothing** — the rows stay attached to the hidden collection, vanish from every count because `P6-110` filters it out, and return intact on undo. Return a `DeleteCollectionReceipt { collection_id, move_ids, reparented }` mirroring `TeardownReceipt` — handles, not counts, because the undo needs them. Inbox stays refused. Follow the `plan_move`/`plan_drop` precedent: a pure planner tested apart from the write. **The regression test that matters most:** a card held *only* in the deleted collection is still `owned` afterwards at its destination, and is *not* owned when discarded — one assertion covering all four former "owned" definitions. **Prereq: `P6-110`.**
